newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-TOP PLAYERS SURVIVE PARIS DEBACLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-TOP PLAYERS SURVIVE PARIS DEBACLE.

text.p: For a tournament that saw 14 seeds tumble by midweek, the Paris Open won by Swede Thomas Enqvist on Sunday had surprisingly little effect on the field for the ATP World Championship in two weeks.

Stuttgart Open winner Boris Becker, Olympic gold medalist Andre Agassi and Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek occupied the three undecided berths before the seeds came into the tournament at Bercy in the second round on Tuesday.

By mid-afternoon on Wednesday all three had lost second round matches and their places appeared to be in jeopardy, especially Agassi's as he had said he was not playing in any more tour tournaments this season.
But with South African Wayne Ferreira losing in the third round at Bercy, the ATP announced that Becker's place in the eight-player World Championship in Hanover starting on November 19 was safe.
Agassi then secured his berth when Krajicek pulled out of the Stockholm Open starting on Monday with a sore knee. The Dutchman remains vulnerable in eighth place.
"The eighth and final spot will be decided next week. (Top seed) Ferreira must reach at least the final in Stockholm in order to overtake Krajicek and qualify," the ATP said.

Several players including Enqvist, who beat Russian Yevgeny Kafelnikov in straight sets in the Bercy final, are vying for the reserve spot in case Krajicek or Austrian Thomas Muster are unable to play in Hanover through injury.
Muster retired from his second round match with Stefan Edberg here after dropping the first set 6-2 suffering from a recurring shoulder problem.
American Todd Martin, seeded second in Stockholm, Chilean Marcelo Rios, who is playing in the Santiago Open, or Enqvist could break in to the reserve berth with good results this week.

Enqvist, a world championship semifinalist last year who is having a fine finish to an otherwise indifferent season, said: "I don't regret anything. If you don't have enough points to be in the championship, you're not good enough to be there.
"I'm very happy to win this (Paris) tournament, my first big tournament."
The Hanover qualifiers so far are world number one Pete Sampras, Michael Chang, Kafelnikov, Goran Ivanisevic, Muster, Becker and Agassi.
